From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@asmartchat.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API evaluation follow-up - quickstart, endpoints, rate limits

Hi Sam -

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Really enjoyed learning about ASmartChat's goals for faster reply suggestions and taxonomy-based routing. Quick recap + proposed next steps below so we can keep momentum: 

Recap:
- You want a fast time-to-value path to validate a generation-based reply assistant (10-20M tokens/month initial volume).
- Primary concerns: latency under 250ms p50 for interactive suggestions, predictable cost, and data isolation requirements (no long-term retention for PII).
- You asked about deployment options: Hosted API for quick evaluation vs Dedicated capacity if throughput/SLA needs increase vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict isolation.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quickstart on Hosted API - I can provision eval credits and a sandbox project so your eng team can hit the endpoints today.
2) Send the quickstart guide (attached) and a short checklist for keys, rate limits, and sample client code.
3) Follow-up call next week with Marissa (solutions engineer) to seed prompts and check perf; if results look good we'll size Dedicated options.

Attached: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf (small, 6 pages) and eval-setup-instructions.txt with curl examples.

Open questions for your team before we set up the sandbox:
- Do you need IP allowlisting / VPC peering for the sandbox?
- Desired concurrency and expected RPS per endpoint (rough ballpark is fine)

I'll cc Marissa to coordinate the technical onboarding. If you're ready, I'll provision credits and share the sandbox link + API key by EOD Monday.

Thanks,

-
Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya - good recap. Couple of quick clarifications before we schedule the sandbox: 

1) Rate limits / concurrency: for the POC we expect ~50 RPS at peak across a single endpoint, but average is around 5-10 RPS. If we scale this to production in Q3, we could go to 300-500 RPS.
2) Latency target: p50 < 250ms, p95 ideally < 600ms. Is Hosted API able to meet that for the base models you showed, assuming standard prompt lengths (avg ~120 tokens input, ~60 tokens generation)?
3) Data isolation: for POC we're fine with Hosted API but need assurance that logs/inputs aren't retained beyond 30 days and that we can opt-out of logging. Can you confirm retention options?

Also curious about the endpoints: you mentioned streaming and non-streaming options - which SDK examples should we use for a web real-time UX?

If you can answer these we'll confirm a 30-45 minute onboarding slot with our eng lead (Asha).

- Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Product, ASmartChat

Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation follow-up - quickstart, endpoints, rate limits

Hi Sam / Asha -

Great questions - answers below and next steps.

1) Rate limits / concurrency:
- Sandbox (Hosted API): default soft limit 100 RPS per project; for your POC we can temporarily raise to 200 RPS. Production scaling to 300-500 RPS is commonly handled by Dedicated capacity (reserved pools) or by sharding across projects/endpoints.
- We also provide per-key throttles and adaptive concurrency controls.

2) Latency expectations:
- For the model variants we demoed (redwood-v2-small / redwood-v2-medium) and your prompt profile (~120 tokens in / ~60 out) we typically see p50 between 120-220ms and p95 ~450-700ms on Hosted API in us-west regions with standard instance routing.
- If consistent sub-250ms p50 at scale is required, Dedicated capacity gives tighter SLOs and custom instance selection. We can run a 48-hour perf test from your region to capture realistic numbers.

3) Data retention / logging:
- Hosted API default: short-term logs for debugging retained 30 days. We offer an opt-out for logging/retention for evaluation projects; we can turn logging off for your sandbox and set retention to 0-7 days. Private (VPC/on-prem) allows full customer control over logs.

Endpoints / SDK for realtime UX:
- For web real-time UX we recommend the streaming endpoint + our JS SDK (examples in the attached quickstart and at https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstart/hosted-api#streaming).
- Non-streaming (batch) endpoints are better for background processing such as nightly reranks/embeddings.

Attachments and resources:
- redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf - step-by-step onboarding, curl/JS examples, and recommended timeout/retry settings.
- eval-setup-instructions.txt - one-line commands to create project, generate key, and run example load tests.

Next steps I will take now:
- Provision sandbox project with 10k eval credits and raise sandbox RPS to 200 for 7 days.
- Share sandbox API key and the quickstart docs (expected by EOD PDT).

Propose we schedule a 30-minute onboarding call with your eng lead Asha and Marissa on Wed or Thu next week - available windows: Wed 10-11am PT, Thu 1-3pm PT. Which works for you?

If you want Dedicated sizing info ahead of the perf test I can include expected monthly commit ranges and latency uplift tradeoffs.

Thanks,

-
